questions.q: A snail crawls 2/7 m every minute. How far does it crawl in 4 minutes?
questions.a: 8/7 m, because 4 × 2/7 = 2/7 + 2/7 + 2/7 + 2/7 = 8/7 m; only the numerator is multiplied by 4.

questions.q: Which steps find 3/8 × 40 by the method the chapter uses for a fraction times a whole number?
o: Divide 40 by 8, then multiply the result by 3
Divide 40 by 3, then multiply the result by 8
Multiply 40 by 8, then divide the result by 3
Add 3 and 8, then multiply the result by 40
questions.a: Divide 40 by 8, then multiply the result by 3: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 and 3 × 5 = 15, so 3/8 × 40 = 15.

questions.q: Match each product in Column I with its value in Column II. Column I: 1. 3 × 2/9; 2. 5 × 3/10; 3. 2/3 × 12; 4. 3/4 × 6. Column II: P. 2/3; Q. 3/2; R. 8; S. 9/2.
Assertion (A): 2 1/4 × 3 = 6 3/4. Reason (R): To multiply a mixed fraction by a whole number, multiply only the whole-number part (2 × 3) and keep the fraction part 1/4 as it is.
o: A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: A is true, but R is false: 2 1/4 = 9/4 and 9/4 × 3 = 27/4 = 6 3/4. The method in R would give 6 1/4, because it forgets to multiply the 1/4 by 3 as well.

questions.q: Farida walks 4/5 km to school every day. (a) How far does she walk to school in 6 days? (b) Write your answer as a mixed fraction.
True or False: Ravi says 7 × 2/3 = 14/21, because he multiplied both the numerator and the denominator by 7.
s: States that the claim is False
Gives the correct product 7 × 2/3 = 14/3 = 4 2/3 and notes that 14/21 is just 2/3 again, since only the numerator is multiplied
questions.a: False. 7 × 2/3 = 14/3 = 4 2/3. Multiplying both numerator and denominator by 7 gives 14/21, which equals 2/3, so the size has not changed at all.

questions.q: Change each mixed fraction to an improper fraction, multiply, and give the answer as a mixed fraction: (a) 1 2/5 × 3 (b) 4 × 2 1/3 (c) 3 3/4 × 2

A school kitchen in Lucknow uses 3/4 kg of dal every day. (a) How much dal does it use in 5 days? (b) Write that answer as a mixed fraction. (c) How much dal does it use in 12 days? (d) The kitchen had 10 kg of dal at the start of those 12 days. How much is left at the end? (e) Dal costs ₹120 per kg. What does one day's dal cost?

Ganga runs a tea stall at the bus stand in Madurai. Every glass of tea she makes uses 1/6 litre of milk. On Monday she sold 30 glasses in the morning and 18 glasses in the evening. She buys milk at ₹60 per litre, and her milk comes in cans that hold 2 1/2 litres each. (a) How much milk did she use in the morning? (b) How much milk did she use in the evening? (c) What did the milk for the whole day cost her? (d) Would 3 cans of milk have been enough for Monday? Show why.
s: (d) 3 × 5/2 = 15/2 = 7 1/2 litres, which is less than 8 litres, so 3 cans are not enough (short by 1/2 litre)
questions.a: (a) 5 litres (b) 3 litres (c) ₹480 (d) No: 3 cans hold 7 1/2 litres, which is 1/2 litre less than the 8 litres needed.

questions.q: To show 1/3 × 1/5 on a unit square, the square is cut into 3 equal parts one way and 5 equal parts the other way. Into how many equal small parts is the whole square cut?
questions.a: 15, because 3 × 5 = 15 equal parts, so one part is 1/15 of the whole and 1/3 × 1/5 = 1/15.

questions.q: A unit square is cut into 4 equal rows and 3 equal columns. A block 1 row tall and 2 columns wide is shaded. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The shaded block shows 1/4 × 2/3 = 2/12: the whole has 4 × 3 = 12 equal parts and 1 × 2 = 2 of them are shaded, which is 1/6 in lowest form.

questions.q: Consider the statements. Statement I: 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/12. Statement II: A rectangle 1/2 m long and 1/4 m wide has an area of 1/8 square metre. Statement III: 1/3 × 1/4 = 1/7. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: I and II only. 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/(2 × 6) = 1/12 and 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8, so I and II are correct; 1/3 × 1/4 = 1/12, not 1/7 (the denominators are multiplied, not added).

questions.q: Notice board A is 3/4 m long and 4/9 m wide. Notice board B is 2/3 m long and 3/5 m wide. Which statement is correct?
o: B is larger: its area is 2/5 square metre against 1/3 square metre
A is larger: its area is 1/3 square metre against 1/5 square metre
A is larger, because it has the longest side, 3/4 m
They are equal, because each has one side shorter than 3/4 m
questions.a: B is larger: its area is 2/5 square metre against 1/3 square metre. Area of A = 3/4 × 4/9 = 12/36 = 1/3; area of B = 2/3 × 3/5 = 6/15 = 2/5; and 2/5 = 6/15 is more than 1/3 = 5/15.

questions.q: (a) Into how many equal parts is a unit square divided to show 1/6 × 1/7? (b) Write the value of 1/6 × 1/7.
questions.a: (a) 42 equal parts (b) 1/42

questions.q: A rectangular cloth piece for a school banner is 3/5 m long and 5/8 m wide. (a) Find its area in lowest form. (b) Four such pieces are stitched together without overlap. Find their total area.
questions.a: (a) 3/8 square metre (b) 1 1/2 square metres

questions.q: Anil says, 'A rectangle with sides 2/3 m and 3/4 m has the same area as a strip with sides 1/2 m and 1 m.' (a) Find both areas. (b) Is Anil right? (c) Find the other side of a third rectangle with one side 5/8 m that has this same area.
s: (b) Yes, Anil is right: both areas are 1/2 square metre
questions.a: (a) Both are 1/2 square metre. (b) Yes, Anil is right. (c) 4/5 m, since 5/8 × 4/5 = 1/2.

questions.q: Bhāskara I explained the product of two unit fractions by dividing a square into rectangles. A unit square is cut into 5 equal columns and 4 equal rows. (a) How many small parts are there, and what fraction of the whole is one part? (b) A block 3 columns wide and 1 row tall is shaded. What fraction of the whole is shaded? (c) Which product does the block in (b) show? (d) A block 3 columns wide and 2 rows tall is shaded instead. Write the shaded fraction in lowest form.
s: (a) 5 × 4 = 20 parts; one part is 1/20 of the whole

questions.q: The Class 7 eco-club of a school in Shillong looks after a farm of area 1 square unit. They plant spinach on a rectangular patch 3/4 unit long and 2/3 unit wide, and carrots on a separate rectangular patch 2/5 unit long and 5/8 unit wide. The patches do not overlap. The club now wants to add a flower bed on the land that is still free. Plan P is a bed 3/5 unit by 1/2 unit; Plan Q is a bed 2/3 unit by 1/3 unit. (a) Find the area of the spinach patch. (b) Find the area of the carrot patch. (c) What area of the farm is still free? (d) Compare each plan's area with the free area. Whose area is small enough for the free land, P's or Q's?
s: (d) P needs 3/5 × 1/2 = 3/10 square unit, more than 1/4 (3/10 = 6/20 > 5/20), so it is too large; Q needs 2/3 × 1/3 = 2/9 square unit, less than 1/4 (8/36 < 9/36), so only Plan Q's area is small enough
questions.a: (a) 1/2 square unit (b) 1/4 square unit (c) 1/4 square unit (d) Only Plan Q's area is small enough: it needs 2/9 square unit, which is less than the free 1/4; Plan P needs 3/10, which is more than 1/4.

questions.q: Brahmagupta stated a formula for multiplying a/b by c/d. Which is it?
questions.a: (a × c)/(b × d): the product of the numerators divided by the product of the denominators.

questions.q: What is 4/9 × 3/8 in lowest form?
questions.a: 1/6: cancel 4 with 8 (leaving 1 and 2) and 3 with 9 (leaving 1 and 3), so the product is (1 × 1)/(3 × 2) = 1/6.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 7 × 2/5 can be worked out as 7/1 × 2/5 = 14/5. Reason (R): A whole number can be written as a fraction with denominator 1.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: writing 7 as 7/1 lets Brahmagupta's formula give (7 × 2)/(1 × 5) = 14/5.

questions.q: A printer uses 14/45 of an ink cartridge every hour. It runs for 15/28 of an hour. What fraction of the cartridge does it use?
questions.a: 1/6: 14/45 × 15/28; cancel 14 with 28 (leaving 1 and 2) and 15 with 45 (leaving 1 and 3), giving 1/(3 × 2) = 1/6.

questions.q: (a) Find 5/6 × 9/10 by cancelling common factors first. (b) Check your answer by multiplying straight across and then reducing.
s: (b) 45/60, which reduces by 15 to 3/4, the same answer
questions.a: (a) 3/4 (b) 45/60 = 3/4, so both ways agree.

questions.q: True or False: To find 10 × 7/15, Meera writes the whole number 10 as 10/1, cancels 10 with 15 by their common factor 5, and gets 14/3.
s: States that the claim is True
questions.a: True. Writing 10 as 10/1 makes it a fraction, so 10 (a numerator) and 15 (a denominator) can be cancelled by 5: (2 × 7)/(1 × 3) = 14/3, the same as 70/15 in lowest form.

questions.q: Multiply and give each answer in lowest form: (a) 2/3 × 3/7 (b) 6 × 5/12 (c) 3/10 × 5/9

A school collects waste paper for recycling. 9/10 of the paper collected is clean. 5/6 of the clean paper is sold to a mill, and the mill turns 8/15 of the paper it buys into notebook paper. (a) What fraction of the collected paper is sold to the mill? (b) What fraction of the collected paper becomes notebook paper? (c) The school collects 450 kg. How many kg become notebook paper? (d) Aman says more than half of the collected paper becomes notebook paper, because each fraction used is more than one half. Is he right? Explain.
s: (d) No: 2/5 is less than 1/2; multiplying by fractions between 0 and 1 makes the result smaller each time, so it can fall below 1/2 even though each fraction is above 1/2
questions.a: (a) 3/4 (b) 2/5 (c) 180 kg (d) No. 2/5 is less than 1/2: each multiplication by a fraction less than 1 shrinks the amount, so three fractions above one half can still give a product below one half.

questions.q: The floor of a school hall is a rectangle 45/4 m long and 32/5 m wide. (a) Find the area of the floor, cancelling common factors first. (b) A carpet covers 5/8 of the floor. Find the carpeted area. (c) The carpet costs ₹240 per square metre. Find its cost. (d) Mats cover 2/9 of the floor that is not carpeted. Find the area under mats. (e) What fraction of the whole floor is bare (no carpet and no mat)? Give it in lowest form.
s: (a) 45/4 × 32/5: cancel 45 with 5 and 32 with 4, giving 9 × 8 = 72 square metres
(d) Not carpeted: 72 − 45 = 27 square metres; 2/9 × 27 = 6 square metres
(e) Bare: 27 − 6 = 21 square metres, which is 21/72 = 7/24 of the floor
questions.a: (a) 72 square metres (b) 45 square metres (c) ₹10,800 (d) 6 square metres (e) 7/24

questions.q: Without multiplying, which product is less than both of the numbers being multiplied?
questions.a: 2/3 × 4/5, because both numbers lie between 0 and 1, and then the product is less than both.

questions.q: Consider the statements. Statement I: 7/4 × 9/5 is greater than both 7/4 and 9/5. Statement II: 2/3 × 9/2 is less than 2/3, because we multiplied by a fraction. Statement III: 5/6 × 3/10 = 3/10 × 5/6. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: I and III only. I is correct because both numbers are greater than 1. II is wrong: 2/3 × 9/2 = 3, which lies between 2/3 and 9/2. III is correct because the order of multiplication does not change the product.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 11/12 × 13/12 is less than 13/12. Reason (R): When one of the numbers being multiplied is between 0 and 1, the product is less than the other number.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: 11/12 lies between 0 and 1, so the product (143/144) is less than the other number, 13/12.

questions.q: For which pair of numbers is the product BOTH greater than one of the numbers and less than the other, AND a whole number?
questions.a: 3/4 and 8: the product is 6, a whole number lying between 3/4 and 8. 5/2 × 4/3 = 10/3 is not whole and is greater than both; 3/2 × 4 = 6 is greater than both; 2/3 × 3/4 = 1/2 is less than both.

questions.q: (a) Find 4/3 × 5/2. (b) Is the product greater than both numbers, less than both, or between them? Give the reason.
s: (b) Greater than both, because both 4/3 and 5/2 are greater than 1
questions.a: (a) 10/3 (b) Greater than both numbers, since both are greater than 1.

questions.q: A rope is 18/5 m long. Juhi cuts off a piece that is 5/6 of the rope. Sanju says the piece must be longer than 18/5 m, because multiplying always makes a number bigger. (a) Find the length of the piece. (b) Explain why it must be shorter than 18/5 m.
s: (b) 5/6 lies between 0 and 1, so the product is less than the other number, 18/5
questions.a: (a) 3 m (b) Multiplying by 5/6, a number between 0 and 1, gives less than 18/5 m; Sanju's rule only holds when the multiplier is greater than 1.

questions.q: Neeraj says, 'If I multiply 8 by any fraction, the answer is less than 8.' (a) Test his claim with 3/4 × 8 and with 5/4 × 8. (b) Is Neeraj right, wrong, or partly right? (c) Rewrite his statement so that it is always true.
s: (b) Partly right: 6 is less than 8, but 10 is more than 8
(c) Multiplying 8 by a fraction between 0 and 1 gives less than 8; by a fraction greater than 1 gives more than 8
questions.a: (a) 6 and 10 (b) Partly right (c) The answer is less than 8 only when the fraction is between 0 and 1; when the fraction is greater than 1, the answer is more than 8.

questions.q: Ishita's screen time is 15/4 hours a day. Her parents offer two plans. Plan A: multiply her daily screen time by 2/3 this week, then multiply the new time by 3/2 next week. Plan B: multiply it by 3/4 this week, then multiply the new time by 3/4 again next week. (a) Find her daily time after each week under Plan A. (b) Find her daily time after each week under Plan B. (c) Which plan leaves her with less screen time at the end? (d) Explain, without working it out again, why Plan A ends where it started. (e) Ishita wants to end below 2 hours a day by multiplying twice by the same fraction, chosen from 3/4, 2/3 and 4/5. Which of these works? Show the checks.
s: (c) Plan B, since 135/64 h (just over 2 h) is less than 15/4 h
(d) The order of multiplication does not matter, so 15/4 × 2/3 × 3/2 = 15/4 × (2/3 × 3/2) = 15/4 × 1
(e) 3/4 twice gives 135/64 h (over 2), 4/5 twice gives 12/5 h (over 2), 2/3 twice gives 15/4 × 4/9 = 5/3 h (under 2); only 2/3 works
questions.a: (a) 5/2 h, then 15/4 h (b) 45/16 h, then 135/64 h (c) Plan B (d) 2/3 × 3/2 = 1, and the order of multiplying does not matter, so she is multiplied by 1 overall. (e) Only 2/3, giving 5/3 h.

questions.q: What is the reciprocal of 5/8?
questions.a: 8/5, because the reciprocal swaps the numerator and denominator, and 5/8 × 8/5 = 1.

questions.q: Using the reciprocal of the divisor, what is 3/4 ÷ 2/5?
Match each division in Column I with its quotient in Column II. Column I: 1. 1 ÷ 1/3; 2. 2 ÷ 1/2; 3. 1/2 ÷ 2; 4. 1/3 ÷ 1/6. Column II: P. 3; Q. 4; R. 1/4; S. 2.
A bench 9/2 m long is painted in equal sections, each 3/8 m long. Which missing-factor sentence matches this, and how many sections are there?
(a) Rewrite 1 ÷ 3/7 as a multiplication with a missing factor. (b) Find the missing factor.
True or False: Dividing 5/6 by 2 gives the same answer as multiplying 5/6 by 1/2.
s: States that the claim is True
Gives the reason: the reciprocal of the divisor 2 is 1/2, so 5/6 ÷ 2 = 5/6 × 1/2 = 5/12
questions.a: True. To divide by 2 we multiply by its reciprocal 1/2; both give 5/12.

questions.q: Divide using Brahmagupta's formula a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c, and give each answer in lowest form: (a) 2/9 ÷ 4/3 (b) 6 ÷ 3/5 (c) 7/8 ÷ 7

Priya works out 4/15 ÷ 8/9 and writes 4/15 × 8/9 = 32/135. (a) What mistake has she made? (b) Find the correct quotient in lowest form. (c) Check your answer by multiplying it by the divisor. (d) State in words the rule Bhāskara II gave for dividing one fraction by another.
s: (a) She multiplied by the divisor 8/9 instead of by its reciprocal 9/8
(c) 3/10 × 8/9 = 24/90 = 4/15, the dividend, so the answer is right
(d) Dividing one fraction by another is the same as multiplying the first by the reciprocal of the second
questions.a: (a) She did not take the reciprocal of the divisor. (b) 3/10 (c) 3/10 × 8/9 = 4/15. (d) Division of one fraction by another equals multiplying the first by the reciprocal of the second.

questions.q: Two handloom weavers in Pochampally work at steady speeds. Lakshmi weaves 5/2 m of cloth in 3/4 hour. Ravi weaves 7/3 m of cloth in 2/3 hour. (a) How many metres does Lakshmi weave in one hour? (b) How many metres does Ravi weave in one hour? (c) Who is faster, and by how much per hour? (d) How long does Ravi take to weave 14 m? (e) An order of 20 m must be woven within 6 hours by one weaver. Can each weaver finish the 20 m within 6 hours? Who finishes earlier, and how much more could that weaver weave in the 6 hours? Justify.
s: (e) In 6 hours Lakshmi weaves 10/3 × 6 = 20 m and Ravi weaves 7/2 × 6 = 21 m, so both can finish; Ravi finishes earlier and could weave 1 m more in the 6 hours
questions.a: (a) 10/3 m (b) 7/2 m (c) Ravi, by 1/6 m per hour (d) 4 hours (e) Both can finish: Lakshmi weaves exactly 20 m in 6 hours and Ravi weaves 21 m. Ravi finishes earlier and could weave 1 m more.

questions.q: Without dividing, which quotient is greater than 6?
questions.a: 6 ÷ 2/3, because the divisor 2/3 lies between 0 and 1, so the quotient (9) is greater than the dividend 6.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 4/5 ÷ 2 is greater than 4/5. Reason (R): When the divisor is greater than 1, the quotient is less than the dividend.
o: A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
questions.a: A is false, but R is true: 4/5 ÷ 2 = 4/5 × 1/2 = 2/5, which is less than 4/5, exactly as R says for a divisor greater than 1.

questions.q: Consider the statements. Statement I: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, which is greater than 3. Statement II: 1/8 ÷ 1/4 = 1/32. Statement III: Dividing a number by another number greater than 1 gives a quotient greater than the dividend. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: I only. 3 × 4 = 12, so I is correct. II is wrong: 1/8 ÷ 1/4 = 1/8 × 4 = 1/2 (1/32 comes from multiplying instead of dividing). III is wrong: a divisor greater than 1 gives a quotient less than the dividend.

questions.q: Asha divides 9/4 by a fraction d and gets a quotient smaller than 9/4. Which of these could d be?
questions.a: 5/3: the quotient is less than the dividend only when the divisor is greater than 1, and 5/3 is the only choice greater than 1 (9/4 ÷ 5/3 = 27/20).

questions.q: (a) Find 5/3 ÷ 5/6 and 5/3 ÷ 10/3. (b) Which quotient is greater than the dividend 5/3? Link your answer to the size of the divisor.
s: (b) 5/3 ÷ 5/6 = 2 is greater than 5/3, because its divisor 5/6 is between 0 and 1; the divisor 10/3 is greater than 1, so that quotient is smaller
questions.a: (a) 2 and 1/2 (b) 5/3 ÷ 5/6, because 5/6 is less than 1.

questions.q: True or False: Since 3/4 is less than 1, dividing 2/3 by 3/4 gives a quotient smaller than 2/3.
s: States that the claim is False
Shows 2/3 ÷ 3/4 = 2/3 × 4/3 = 8/9, which is greater than 2/3, because a divisor between 0 and 1 makes the quotient larger than the dividend
questions.a: False. 2/3 ÷ 3/4 = 8/9, which is greater than 2/3: dividing by a number between 0 and 1 gives a quotient greater than the dividend.

questions.q: Gita says, 'Dividing always makes a number smaller, so 7/2 ÷ 7/8 must be less than 7/2.' (a) Find 7/2 ÷ 7/8. (b) Is Gita right? (c) State the correct rule about when a quotient is smaller than the dividend.
s: (c) The quotient is less than the dividend only when the divisor is greater than 1; a divisor between 0 and 1 gives a larger quotient
questions.a: (a) 4 (b) No, 4 > 3 1/2. (c) A quotient is smaller than the dividend only when the divisor is greater than 1.

questions.q: (a) Without dividing, arrange these quotients in increasing order and give your reasons: 10 ÷ 5/4, 10 ÷ 1, 10 ÷ 4/5, 10 ÷ 2/5. (b) Work out the smallest and the largest to check your order.
s: (a) Divisor 5/4 is greater than 1, so 10 ÷ 5/4 is less than 10; 10 ÷ 1 = 10; divisors 4/5 and 2/5 are below 1, so those quotients are above 10
(a) The smaller divisor gives the larger quotient (2/5 < 4/5), so the order is 10 ÷ 5/4, 10 ÷ 1, 10 ÷ 4/5, 10 ÷ 2/5

questions.q: For the Uttarayan kite festival in Ahmedabad, Imran has a roll of 30 m of manja thread. Each small kite needs 5/4 m of thread to tie its bridle and each large kite needs 5/2 m. His sister Zoya says that dividing 30 by 5/4 must give more than 30 kites, because 5/4 is a fraction. (a) How many small kites can Imran tie with all the thread? (b) How many large kites can he tie with all the thread? (c) Explain why Zoya is wrong without doing the division. (d) Imran wants exactly 10 large kites and then as many small kites as possible. How many kites does he get in all?
s: (c) The divisor 5/4 is greater than 1, so the quotient must be less than the dividend 30
(d) 10 large kites use 10 × 5/2 = 25 m; the 5 m left makes 5 ÷ 5/4 = 4 small kites; 14 kites in all
questions.a: (a) 24 (b) 12 (c) 5/4 is greater than 1, so 30 ÷ 5/4 is less than 30. (d) 10 large + 4 small = 14 kites.

questions.q: Half of the 40 students in a class are girls, and 1/4 of the girls play in the school band. How many girls play in the band?

Match each problem in Column I with its answer in Column II. Column I: 1. Number of square bricks of side 1/3 unit needed to cover 2 square units; 2. Litres of milk in each cup when 1/2 litre is shared equally among 4 cups; 3. 1/3 of 1/2 of 1/4 of 48 cowrie shells; 4. Number of times two fountains together fill a cistern in one day, if one alone fills it in 1/2 day and the other in 1/3 day. Column II: P. 18; Q. 1/8; R. 2; S. 5.

One round of the walking track in a Bengaluru park is 5/8 km. (a) Kavya walks 6 1/2 rounds. How far does she walk? Give a mixed fraction. (b) Her goal is 5 km. How many rounds make exactly 5 km? (c) How many more rounds must she walk after her 6 1/2 rounds to reach the goal?
questions.a: (a) 4 1/16 km (b) 8 rounds (c) 1 1/2 rounds

questions.q: The textbook suggests these rates for old Indian coins: 1 silver dramma = 4 copper panas and 1 copper pana = 30 cowrie shells. (a) How many cowrie shells make 1 dramma at these rates? (b) What fraction of a dramma is 1 cowrie shell? (c) In Bhāskarāchārya's tale the miser gave 1/1280 of a dramma. At the rates above, is that even one whole cowrie shell? Show the working.
s: (c) 1/1280 × 120 = 120/1280 = 3/32 cowrie, which is less than one shell (the tale's 1 cowrie used the rate 1 dramma = 1280 cowries)
questions.a: (a) 120 (b) 1/120 of a dramma (c) No: 1/1280 of a dramma is only 3/32 of a cowrie shell at these rates.

questions.q: A family from Pune travels 360 km to visit relatives. They cover 5/12 of the whole distance by bus. The distance they cover by train is 3/5 of the bus distance. The rest is by taxi. (a) How many km do they travel by bus? (b) What fraction of the whole journey is by train, and how many km is that? (c) What fraction of the whole journey is by taxi, and how many km? (d) Their uncle says they went farther by taxi than by bus. Is he right? Explain.
s: (d) No: the taxi part is 1/3 (120 km), less than the bus part 5/12 (150 km)
questions.a: (a) 150 km (b) 1/4 of the journey, 90 km (c) 1/3 of the journey, 120 km (d) No, taxi 120 km < bus 150 km.

questions.q: A school has 9 kg of coloured powder for a Republic Day rangoli contest. Each team is given 3/4 kg. (a) How many teams can take part? (b) The judges first keep aside 1/6 of the powder for decorating the stage. How many teams can take part now? (c) In plan (b), each team actually uses only 2/3 of its share. How much powder is left unused by all the teams together? (d) How much powder does one team actually use? (e) The teacher proposes giving each team only what it uses, from the powder left after the judges' share. How many teams can then take part? Is this a better plan? Justify.
s: (c) Each team leaves 1/3 of 3/4 = 1/4 kg; 10 × 1/4 = 5/2 kg unused
(e) 15/2 ÷ 1/2 = 15 teams; better, since 5 more teams can play and no powder is wasted
questions.a: (a) 12 teams (b) 10 teams (c) 2 1/2 kg (d) 1/2 kg (e) 15 teams; better, because 5 more teams take part and nothing is wasted.

questions.q: A village in Barmer, Rajasthan, gets one water tanker of 6000 litres every day. At present 2/5 of the water goes to the school, 1/4 of the remaining water goes to the health centre, and the rest is shared equally by the 50 homes of the village. The panchayat is considering a new plan: the school gets 1/3 of the water, the health centre still gets 1/4 of what remains, and the rest is shared equally by the 50 homes. (a) Under the present plan, how many litres go to the school and to the health centre? (b) How many litres does each home get under the present plan? (c) How many litres does each home get under the new plan? (d) Should the panchayat adopt the new plan? Give one gain and one loss, using your numbers.
s: (c) School 2000 L, remaining 4000 L, health centre 1000 L, homes 3000 L; 3000 ÷ 50 = 60 L each
(d) A justified decision: each home gains 6 L a day and the health centre gains 100 L, but the school loses 400 L a day
questions.a: (a) School 2400 L, health centre 900 L (b) 54 L (c) 60 L (d) Either choice with reasons: homes gain 6 L each and the health centre 100 L, while the school loses 400 L.
